Cerebral Vascular Accident (CVA) or stroke, results when an artery supplying the brain, is blocked. Like a heart attack, a
blockage will cause a “Cerebral Infarct”.

Blood Brain Barrier

BBB isolates the neural tissue of the CNS, from the general circulation, the result of endothelial
cells lining the brain capillaries, and Astrocytes

Endothelia - are strongly connected and regulate diffusion of materials between them
Astrocytes  - help to determine the permeability of the endothelial cells (via release of specific
chemicals)

Permitted, to cross - lipid-soluble compounds, lipids such as steroids, small alcohols, oxygen,
ammonia and carbon dioxide
Water soluble compounds, often require active transport

The BBB is complete, through out the CNS, however, there are 4 areas of exception
a. Hypothalamus, to allow circulation of hormones to and from the hypothalamus
b. posterior capillaries of Pituitary - permeable, allowing release/uptake of ADH and Oxytocin
c. capillaries in Pineal Gland - permeable, allowing the endocrine secretions of the Pineal Gland,
to enter our circulation (Melatonin – sleep rhythms)
d. Capillaries of Choroid Plexuses - very permeable to maintain the CSF

Blood CSF Barrier – another barrier created by specialized Ependymal cells surrounding the
capillaries of the Choroid Plexus

Transport of materials across the BBB and BCSFB is very selective, even with smaller ions.
Because of this selectivity, the CSF, has a slightly different, (from normal circulating blood) but
extremely consistent ph, and ion concentration levels, and the slightest deviation can result in
severe repercussions/illness.
